paragraphs: I'm David Abril Perrig, a software engineer and the founder of Abril Codes, a boutique studio based in Córdoba, Argentina. I design the architecture and write the core of every project: you don't talk to a salesperson, you talk to the engineer building the system.

Three years shipping backends, native mobile apps and self-managed infrastructure for startups and clients across the US and Europe: a geolocated marketplace, a logistics CRM with a C++20 routing engine, point-of-sale systems and autonomous AI agents.
Final-year Software Engineering student at UBP with an 8.75/10 GPA, and a certified electronics technician: I understand the software and the hardware it runs on.
About.aiBody: I use AI as a precision tool, not as a careless code generator. Every architectural decision, every data contract and every system boundary is mine. When AI ships inside a product, it ships with guardrails: in Nightdesk I built a verifier that matches every quote against the source document character by character, and rejects the draft when it doesn't exist.

orion-logistics.title: OrionLogistics
orion-logistics.description: A B2B logistics ecosystem: offline-first Android app, NestJS backend, live-map web dashboard and a custom C++20 routing engine.
orion-logistics.longDescription:
Are your drivers guessing their routes, losing time, with no way to prove what was actually delivered? OrionLogistics fixes that.

An Android app every driver carries that:
• Organizes and optimizes routes automatically
• Records each delivery with photos, signatures and notes as hard evidence
• Captures all customer activity: who, what, when, where
• Prints invoices on the street with portable printers
• Turns the whole operation into clear metrics from day one

The system syncs orders automatically, manages roles (Admin, Driver, Merchandiser) and keeps a complete record of who did what and when. No paper, no excuses.

Real results in live operations:
📦 40% less time on the road
✅ 25% fewer operational errors
🚀 +50 deliveries per day

Under the hood: the app is 100% offline-first, so drivers never lose data in dead zones. Local persistence with Room and a reactive synchronizer built on Coroutines and Flow that queues operations and flushes them in chronological order the moment connectivity is detected. Routing runs on a custom C++20 engine over Vroom and OSRM, solving TSP and time-windowed routing problems (CVRP/VRPTW) in milliseconds.

cappy.title: Cappy
cappy.description: A geolocated trades marketplace: React Native with Expo, Node backend on PostgreSQL + PostGIS and in-app payments via MercadoPago.
cappy.longDescription:
Finding a plumber, an electrician or a gas fitter is still a matter of group chats and loose recommendations. Cappy turns it into an actual marketplace.

A mobile app that:
• Shows available professionals based on your exact location, in real time
• Lets each worker draw their own coverage radius on the map
• Verifies certifications and reviews before you hire anyone
• Charges inside the app through MercadoPago, no blind transfers

The real challenge was twofold: low-latency proximity matching, and cutting the friction out of worker onboarding so the marketplace had supply from day one.

Under the hood: geospatial matching is solved by PostgreSQL with PostGIS using ST_DWithin queries, so search scales without recomputing distances in memory. The app is React Native with Expo SDK 52, Expo Router and Zustand, with Mapbox maps that keep responding offline. Co-developed with Santiago.

nightdesk.title: Nightdesk
nightdesk.description: A multi-agent Python system that researches and writes autonomously, with a verifier that checks every quote against its source.
nightdesk.longDescription:
The problem with using AI to write isn't bad prose: it's fabrication. Nightdesk attacks that with mechanical verification, not with more prompting.

It's an autonomous newsroom where several agents:
• Research and build an indexed corpus of sources
• Synthesize and write complete pieces
• Pass through an independent fact-checker before anything ships

The key is algorithmic grounding: the verifier takes every quote and searches for it character by character in the original document, using exact normalized substring matching. If the quote doesn't literally exist in the source, the draft is rejected. There's no room for the model to round a number.

Under the hood: Python 3.11 with Pydantic v2 for typed data contracts, an async event bus, a DAG-based scheduler with preemption for breaking news, and a finite state machine governing each draft's immutable lifecycle. SQLite with FTS5 indexes for source search, a watchdog pattern for hung agents and a circuit breaker for external API failures.

pos.title: B2B POS System
pos.description: Point of sale and real-time inventory control: Java 21 with Spring Boot 3, Next.js frontend, invoicing, roles and stock auditing.
pos.longDescription:
Businesses moving stock across several locations usually discover the gaps when it's already too late. This system surfaces them as they happen.

It covers the full operation:
• Sales with invoicing and real-time stock control
• Product catalog with instant search
• User roles and per-operation permissions
• Profitability reports and an audit trail on every stock movement

Measured result: 20% fewer inventory discrepancies.

Under the hood: a Java 21 backend with Spring Boot 3.2, Spring Data JPA and Spring Security with JWT, layered architecture and strict ACID transaction handling on every sale — a sale is never left half-written — documented with OpenAPI. Next.js frontend with Material UI and TypeScript, deployed on GCP and Azure.

hipolito.title: Hipólito Educational Chat
hipolito.description: An educational browser adventure with an AI tutor running 100% on the student's device: no servers, no token cost.
hipolito.longDescription:
A narrative educational game where kids talk to a virtual tutor. The interesting part isn't the chat: it's where it runs.

The language model executes entirely inside the browser, on the user's machine. That means:
• Zero data sent to external servers: full privacy
• Zero API cost per conversation, no matter how many students use it
• It works even when the classroom connection drops

It's the proof that generative AI can reach a school without a monthly bill tied to usage.

Under the hood: the Xenova/LaMini-Flan-T5-248M model running through Transformers.js over WebAssembly, embedded in a game compiled with RenPyWeb to HTML5 Canvas. Served with Node, Express and Caddy.

simpleloc.title: SimpleLoc
simpleloc.description: A native iOS GPS tracker for the outdoors: works without signal, caches maps locally and protects battery. Swift, SwiftUI and CoreLocation.
simpleloc.longDescription:
In the mountains there's no signal, and battery is finite. SimpleLoc is built on those two truths.

The app:
• Records your entire trek with no cellular connection
• Caches maps locally before you leave
• Imports and replays routes from GPX files
• Stretches battery life with adaptive throttling of GPS reads

Under the hood: native Swift and SwiftUI with CoreLocation, adjusting sampling frequency to the user's actual movement instead of polling the GPS at a constant rate. Ships with an equivalent Android client in Kotlin.

miscuentas.title: MisCuentas
miscuentas.description: Multi-currency personal finance in Python: category budgets, historical exchange rates and 29 tests guarding every cent.
miscuentas.longDescription:
Tracking money in two currencies under inflation breaks any spreadsheet. MisCuentas solves it with historical rates: every entry is stored at the value of the day it happened, not today's.

It includes:
• Category budgets and projected balances
• Automatic currency conversion
• Full data isolation between users

Under the hood: Python 3.11 with Flask and SQLAlchemy 2 on SQLite in WAL mode, with schema-level triggers and CHECK constraints — integrity doesn't depend on the application behaving. 29 automated pytest tests covering the monetary calculations.

web-epica.title: Web Épica
web-epica.description: 3D frontend experiments: Three.js and React Three Fiber held at 60 FPS in the browser, on Astro, GSAP and Tailwind 4.
web-epica.longDescription:
A personal lab for pushing what a browser can do without dropping frames.

Interactive three-dimensional scenes, micro-interactions and transitions sustained at 60 FPS, built with Three.js and React Three Fiber on Astro and React 19, with GSAP and Framer Motion for choreography and Tailwind CSS v4 for the visual system.

It's the test bench where I validate performance techniques before taking them into a client project.
